data.plain: Making an irreversible change without an undo step, a rollback record, a compare-and-swap or world-version guard, or an explicit declaration that it cannot be undone.

analogy.boundary: The picture covers only one transfer; setting up a recall and a balance check for it does nothing for the bank's other payments.

maps.analogy: either a recall option or a note in advance that this transfer cannot be reversed
maps.doctrine: an undo step or a declared point of no return

maps.analogy: checking the balance still matches what you saw before you send
maps.doctrine: the compare-and-swap check against the expected parent state

maps.analogy: two people moving money out of the same account at once
maps.doctrine: two writers racing on the same path

analogy.text: Sending a bank transfer that cannot be recalled without first checking that the balance has not changed since you last looked.

reader.counterexample: A step writes straight over a shared path assuming the previous state still holds, with no compare-and-swap and no undo, and silently overwrites another writer's change.
reader.does_not_prove: These safeguards cover the named landing paths and leave every other write in the system as it was.

example.text: The work-landing replay refuses to continue when the expected parent commit has moved or the head was not advanced as recorded, so a multi-step change cannot land on top of a state that has already changed.

reader.governs: Every change written to shared state.
reader.plain: The mistake of making a real change that is hard to undo while assuming it can be undone, when nothing was set up to undo it and nothing checked that the situation had not already moved.
reader.potential_misread: That because the normal case works, any change can be undone later if something goes wrong.
reader.refuses: Writing an irreversible change with no undo step, no rollback record, no compare-and-swap or version check, and no declared point of no return.
reader.requires: Either a way to undo the change or a declared point of no return, a compare-and-swap against the expected parent for multi-step changes, and one writer per path.
reader.why_it_matters: It stops a change from silently overwriting someone else's work or stopping halfway with no record of how to undo it.
